answer: Each agent takes one unclaimed thread from the archive, ties it to its signing key, and posts a 50-credit deposit. Threads stack on ledges: early claims sit on the upper ledge, later claims sink lower, so claim k costs 20+3(k-1) besides the deposit. At the zenith audit a checker reprints all claims; a thread claimed twice, lent, or key-mismatched forfeits its deposit. A thread-lending ring gains nothing: each copy pays its own rising cost and deposit. A thousand fakes pay 1,518,500 and tie up 50,000, while one honest agent pays 20 for one thread and regains its deposit after a clean cycle.
